author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read N-central audit records from Administration > Audit Export. N-central sends them to the data collector over TCP, through a TLS syslog relay for hosted N-central. Logins, logouts and failed logins go to Auth, and every other audit record goes to CloudAudit.
notes:
Setup:
- Turn on Administration > Audit Export (the Compliance permission) and send to the data collector over TCP: N-central has no UDP option.
- On premises, use port 601 with TLS off when the collector is on the same network.
- Hosted N-central only sends TCP 6514 with TLS and a CA-signed certificate, which the data collector's documented ports (UDP 514, TCP 601) don't include, so run a TLS syslog relay that forwards to the collector; a relay that adds its own header in front of the line is fine.

Field mapping:
- Logins, logouts and failed logins go to Auth; every other audit record goes to CloudAudit with the event name, technician, source address and any device or customer named in brackets.
- The parser keys on the layout, not on event ids, and treats an action that says fail as a failed login.

Sources and licenses:
- N-able documents the message layout with two examples and lists the audited events by name, not their event ids or wording.

Made up in the samples:
- The samples use the documented layout, and their event ids (other than login.singlesignon and servicetemplate.create) and action wording are made up.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13 (66 of 66 fields matched the emulator), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- On 2026-10-14 each child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 5 Run Tests.
